text:
eli_sec: Heads-up — our backup-uploader role lost kms:GenerateDataKey permission in last IAM change. CloudTrail alert flagged several PutObject requests to s3://prod-backups without x-amz-server-side-encryption:AWS-KMS.

marta: saw the alert. link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/alerts/alert/12345 — looks like uploads between 02:10-02:22 UTC.

sam: do we have an initial scope? Athena + S3 Inventory should show which prefixes.

jin: quick scan done — ~312 objects in prod-backups/2026-03-20/ that lack SSE-KMS header. I used a head-object loop.

eli_sec: paste of my quick check command:
```
aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket prod-backups --prefix 2026-03-20/ --query 'Contents[].Key' --output text | xargs -n1 -I {} aws s3api head-object --bucket prod-backups --key {} --query '{Key:Key, SSE:ServerSideEncryption, KMS:Metadata.ssekms}'
```
This returned many objects with "ServerSideEncryption": null.

marta: is it only the backup-uploader principal? check CloudTrail principal.

sam: confirmed principal arn:aws:iam::123:role/backup-uploader-prod. PutObject events show no x-amz-server-side-encryption header. Looks like someone removed kms:GenerateDataKey but left PutObject allowed.

jin: immediate mitigation suggestion: temporarily restrict that role or add a bucket policy deny for prod-backups/* until we investigate. I applied a scoped deny to the role for now.

ops-bot: iam-policy change applied by jin at 2333334650 — policy rollback (scoped deny) succeeded.

eli_sec: remediation options brainstorm:
1) in-place re-encrypt via S3 CopyObject with SSE-KMS (fastest, keep keys under KMS).
2) re-upload from original encrypted source if available.
3) run distributed job (Glue/Lambda/Batch) to copy and set SSE.
Consider rate limits, cost, and metadata preservation.

marta: option 1 is simplest: `aws s3 cp s3://prod-backups/foo s3://prod-backups/foo --metadata-directive REPLACE --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:...` — need to preserve user metadata and ACLs. Also capture original ETag/size in audit.

sam: also ensure the actor doing the copy has kms:Encrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey — CMK grants need to be checked.

jin: I'm drafting a runbook: list affected keys, chunk into batches of 100, copy with SSE-KMS, verify checksums, tag with `re-encrypted-by=eng-security`, log each key in SEC-ENC-2026. Will run on a small prefix first.

eli_sec: I'll create a Jira ticket SEC-ENC-2026 and assign to jin + sam. Timeline: scope by EOD (12h), start re-encrypt within 12h after scope, full verification within 36h.

marta: policy change process update: require two approvers for removing KMS permissions and add an automated IAM diff check in deploy pipeline. I'll open a PR template change.

sam: alerting: add a CloudWatch Event / EventBridge rule to detect PutObject to prod-backups without SSE-KMS and send to eng-security Slack + PagerDuty.

jin: on it — will also add an S3 bucket policy that requires `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption` = "aws:kms" for prod-backups. That will prevent future accidental uploads without SSE.

eli_sec: note for remediation: ensure copy jobs run under a principal with CMK access; coordinate with security-kms for a temporary grant if needed.

marta: security-kms, can you grant the runbook role Encrypt/GenerateDataKey for the CMK and add audit annotations?

security-kms: we can create a limited grant for arn:aws:iam::123:role/backup-reencrypt-runner, set an automatic expiry of 48h, and enable key rotation logs. Will do after SEC ticket is created.

ops-bot: ticket created SEC-ENC-2026: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-ENC-2026 (assigned jin, sam)

sam: starting a scoped copy on prefix prod-backups/2026-03-20/test to validate approach. Will monitor downstream services.

jin: test run finished: 20 objects re-encrypted, ETag and sizes match, tags applied. No consumer breakage observed. Logs uploaded to the ticket.

eli_sec: nice. next steps: full re-encrypt run, update IAM PR process, add alert rule + bucket policy, postmortem write-up once closure. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
